grammar.title: Formal circumstance: にあたって
grammar.explanation:
Noun or dictionary verb + にあたって introduces an important occasion and preparations or attitudes appropriate to it. It is common in formal announcements.

Formation: Noun or dictionary verb + にあたって. にあたり is a formal equivalent often used in announcements.

Usage and cautions: This frames a significant undertaking, commencement or occasion, typically with preparation, resolve or a greeting. It is not the ordinary choice for every minor daily action. It concerns facing the occasion, rather than the simple chronological meaning “after”.

examples.ja: 新生活を始めるにあたって、目標を決めました。
examples.en: On starting a new life, I set some goals.

examples.ja: 入学にあたって、必要な書類を確認してください。
examples.reading: にゅうがくにあたって、ひつようなしょるいをかくにんしてください。
examples.en: In preparation for enrollment, please check the necessary documents.

examples.ja: 新事業を始めるにあたって、専門家に相談しました。
examples.reading: しんじぎょうをはじめるにあたって、せんもんかにそうだんしました。
examples.en: On starting a new business, I consulted a specialist.

questions.prompt: Choose a formal 'on the occasion of opening'.
choices: 開店にあたって
開店に限らず
開店に反して
開店を問わず
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “開店にあたって”. にあたって frames an important occasion for an accompanying action.

questions.prompt: Frame a significant departure: 海外赴任＿、家族と話し合った。
choices: に限らず
に反して
にかかわらず
にあたって
questions.explanation: にあたって frames the overseas assignment as the important occasion prompting discussion.

questions.prompt: Which occasion most naturally suits formal にあたって?
choices: A purely accidental sneeze
An object’s color with no event
The opening of a new research institute
Taking one ordinary sip of water
questions.explanation: にあたって typically frames an important undertaking or milestone, such as opening an institute.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 入学にあたって、必要な書類を確認してください。
choices: Please enroll only after losing the documents.
In preparation for enrollment, please check the necessary documents.
After graduating, please discard all documents.
Regardless of enrollment, documents are forbidden.
questions.explanation: “入学にあたって、必要な書類を確認してください。” means “In preparation for enrollment, please check the necessary documents.” in this example. This frames a significant undertaking, commencement or occasion, typically with preparation, resolve or a greeting.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 新事業を始めるにあたって、専門家に相談しました。
choices: On starting a new business, I consulted a specialist.
I started a business despite refusing all advice.
The specialist started a business instead of me.
I consulted a specialist only after closing the business.
questions.explanation: “新事業を始めるにあたって、専門家に相談しました。” means “On starting a new business, I consulted a specialist.” in this example. This frames a significant undertaking, commencement or occasion, typically with preparation, resolve or a greeting.

grammar.title: Only after: て初めて
grammar.explanation:
て初めて emphasizes that an experience or prerequisite makes a realization or outcome possible for the first time.

Formation: Verb て-form + 初めて + realization or newly possible result. 初めて is read はじめて.

Usage and cautions: The first experience is presented as a prerequisite for the later understanding or achievement. This is stronger than merely saying one event happened before another. Distinguish 生まれて初めて, which can mean “for the first time in one’s life”, from this causal realization pattern.

examples.ja: 海外に住んで初めて、家族の大切さが分かりました。
examples.en: Only after living abroad did I appreciate the importance of family.

examples.ja: 親になって初めて、親の苦労が分かりました。
examples.reading: おやになってはじめて、おやのくろうがわかりました。
examples.en: Only after becoming a parent did I understand my parents’ hardships.

examples.ja: 失敗して初めて、準備の大切さに気づきました。
examples.reading: しっぱいしてはじめて、じゅんびのたいせつさにきづきました。
examples.en: Only after failing did I realize the importance of preparation.

questions.prompt: Which emphasizes a realization made only after trying?
choices: やる一方で分かった
やるに反して分かった
やるためだけに分かった
やって初めて分かった
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “やって初めて分かった”. て初めて connects the new understanding to the necessary preceding experience.

questions.prompt: Complete a necessary experience: 自分で作っ＿初めて、難しさが分かった。
choices: たり
ても
て
たらも
questions.explanation: 作って初めて emphasizes that making it personally enabled understanding of its difficulty.

questions.prompt: What relation does 会って初めて安心した emphasize?
choices: The person was met many times after reassurance.
Meeting the person enabled reassurance for the first time.
Reassurance came before the meeting.
Meeting the person prevented reassurance.
questions.explanation: て初めて presents the meeting as the prerequisite that finally made reassurance possible.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 親になって初めて、親の苦労が分かりました。
choices: Only after becoming a parent did I understand my parents’ hardships.
I understood my parents’ hardships before becoming a parent.
I became a parent in order to make life difficult.
My parents first became parents yesterday.
questions.explanation: “親になって初めて、親の苦労が分かりました。” means “Only after becoming a parent did I understand my parents’ hardships.” in this example. The first experience is presented as a prerequisite for the later understanding or achievement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 失敗して初めて、準備の大切さに気づきました。
choices: Careful preparation prevented me from ever failing.
I realized that failure is impossible without preparation.
I prepared for the first time after succeeding.
Only after failing did I realize the importance of preparation.
questions.explanation: “失敗して初めて、準備の大切さに気づきました。” means “Only after failing did I realize the importance of preparation.” in this example. The first experience is presented as a prerequisite for the later understanding or achievement.

grammar.title: Once having done: 以上は
grammar.explanation:
Plain clause + 以上は states that once a fact or commitment holds, a natural duty or determination follows. It is stronger than a neutral reason.

Formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + 以上（は）. Noun / な-adjective commonly use である以上（は）.

Usage and cautions: Once a fact, role or commitment is accepted, a corresponding duty or resolve follows. It is more normative than a neutral “because”. Keep the main clause consistent with that responsibility. The は is optional; the meaning is not numerical “more than” in this use.

examples.ja: 約束した以上は、守らなければなりません。
examples.en: Since I made a promise, I must keep it.

examples.ja: 参加する以上は、最後まで責任を持ちます。
examples.reading: さんかするいじょうは、さいごまでせきにんをもちます。
examples.en: Since I am taking part, I will take responsibility to the end.

examples.ja: 専門家である以上、正確に説明すべきです。
examples.reading: せんもんかであるいじょう、せいかくにせつめいすべきです。
examples.en: As an expert, one should explain accurately.

questions.prompt: Complete a commitment: 引き受けた＿、最後までやる。
choices: ばかりか
ついでに
以上は
ところに
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “以上は”. 以上は treats accepting responsibility as grounds for carrying through.

questions.prompt: Complete a commitment: やると決めた＿、諦めません。
choices: ばかりか
以上は
だけしか
ところへ
questions.explanation: 決めた以上は takes the decision as grounds for the determination not to give up.

questions.prompt: Choose the formal noun connection.
choices: 責任者である以上
責任者の以上
責任者な以上
責任者を以上
questions.explanation: For a noun predicate in this formal construction, 責任者である以上 naturally means since one is the person responsible.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 参加する以上は、最後まで責任を持ちます。
choices: I will take part only after all responsibility ends.
I will avoid responsibility even though I take part.
I participated more than the maximum number of times.
Since I am taking part, I will take responsibility to the end.
questions.explanation: “参加する以上は、最後まで責任を持ちます。” means “Since I am taking part, I will take responsibility to the end.” in this example. Once a fact, role or commitment is accepted, a corresponding duty or resolve follows.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 専門家である以上、正確に説明すべきです。
choices: Someone became an expert after explaining nothing.
An explanation is accurate only if it is short.
As an expert, one should explain accurately.
Experts need not explain accurately.
questions.explanation: “専門家である以上、正確に説明すべきです。” means “As an expert, one should explain accurately.” in this example. Once a fact, role or commitment is accepted, a corresponding duty or resolve follows.

grammar.title: As long as: 限り
grammar.explanation:
Clause + 限り states a condition under which something remains true. 見る限り or 知る限り instead limits the scope of one's evidence.

Formation: Plain clause + 限り（は） for a continuing condition. Nouns / な-adjectives often use である限り; 知る限り limits evidence.

Usage and cautions: Separate two uses: the statement remains true as long as a condition holds, or it is qualified by the scope of one’s knowledge or observation. The latter is not a promise of complete knowledge. ない限り often means unless the stated exception occurs.

examples.ja: 元気である限り、働き続けたいです。
examples.en: As long as I am healthy, I want to keep working.

examples.ja: 時間がある限り、手伝います。
examples.reading: じかんがあるかぎり、てつだいます。
examples.en: I will help as long as I have time.

examples.ja: 私が調べた限りでは、問題はありません。
examples.reading: わたしがしらべたかぎりでは、もんだいはありません。
examples.en: As far as I have investigated, there is no problem.

questions.prompt: What does 私の知る限り limit?
choices: The length of every book I own
The scope of my knowledge
The number of my friends
A strict closing time
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “The scope of my knowledge”. 知る限り qualifies the statement as based only on what the speaker knows.

questions.prompt: Say “unless something unexpected happens”: 何か起きない＿、予定どおり進めます。
choices: 限り
ばかり
たびに
わりに
questions.explanation: 起きない限り means as long as nothing happens, hence unless something happens to change the situation.

questions.prompt: What does 見た限りでは qualify?
choices: A legal maximum viewing time
The number of viewers required
An order to inspect everything
The scope of direct observation
questions.explanation: 見た限りでは limits the claim to what the speaker observed, rather than asserting exhaustive certainty.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 時間がある限り、手伝います。
choices: I have unlimited time to help.
I will help regardless of whether I have time.
I will help as long as I have time.
I will help only after all time has run out.
questions.explanation: “時間がある限り、手伝います。” means “I will help as long as I have time.” in this example. Separate two uses: the statement remains true as long as a condition holds, or it is qualified by the scope of one’s knowledge or observation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 私が調べた限りでは、問題はありません。
choices: I could not investigate because of a problem.
As far as I have investigated, there is no problem.
I guarantee that no problem can ever exist.
My investigation created every problem.
questions.explanation: “私が調べた限りでは、問題はありません。” means “As far as I have investigated, there is no problem.” in this example. Separate two uses: the statement remains true as long as a condition holds, or it is qualified by the scope of one’s knowledge or observation.

grammar.title: Not limited to: に限らず
grammar.explanation:
Noun + に限らず broadens a category: not only that item but others as well. A wider group typically follows.

Formation: Noun + に限らず + broader group, often with も. The following clause expands beyond the initial category.

Usage and cautions: This removes a restriction to one named category. It is not に限り “only” or に限って “precisely on that occasion”. Make the broader inclusion explicit where helpful: 子供に限らず大人も. The relation is additive expansion rather than contrast with expectations.

examples.ja: この店は週末に限らず、平日も混んでいます。
examples.en: This shop is busy not only on weekends but also on weekdays.

examples.ja: この問題は日本に限らず、世界各地で起きています。
examples.reading: このもんだいはにほんにかぎらず、せかいかくちでおきています。
examples.en: This problem occurs not only in Japan but around the world.

examples.ja: 若者に限らず、高齢者にも人気があります。
examples.reading: わかものにかぎらず、こうれいしゃにもにんきがあります。
examples.en: It is popular not only with young people but with older people too.

questions.prompt: Choose broadening beyond students.
choices: 学生に限らず
学生に限って
学生に限り
学生に対してだけ
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “学生に限らず”. に限らず includes people beyond the named category.

questions.prompt: Broaden the category: 会員＿、一般の方も参加できます。
choices: に限り
に反して
に応じて
に限らず
questions.explanation: に限らず explicitly includes nonmembers alongside members; に限り would restrict participation.

questions.prompt: Which continuation fits 日曜日に限らず?
choices: 日曜日以外は必ず休みです。
他の日は一切利用できません。
平日も営業しています。
日曜日だけ営業しています。
questions.explanation: 平日も expands opening days beyond Sunday; the other continuations impose a Sunday-only restriction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この問題は日本に限らず、世界各地で起きています。
choices: The problem cannot occur anywhere in the world.
This problem occurs not only in Japan but around the world.
This problem occurs only in Japan.
Japan has solved this problem for the world.
questions.explanation: “この問題は日本に限らず、世界各地で起きています。” means “This problem occurs not only in Japan but around the world.” in this example. This removes a restriction to one named category.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 若者に限らず、高齢者にも人気があります。
choices: It is popular not only with young people but with older people too.
It is popular only with young people.
Older people dislike it precisely because it is popular.
Neither young nor older people like it.
questions.explanation: “若者に限らず、高齢者にも人気があります。” means “It is popular not only with young people but with older people too.” in this example. This removes a restriction to one named category.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Unexpectedly on that occasion: に限って
grammar.explanation:
に限って can mean especially on this occasion, often an unfortunate exception. With a trusted person it can express disbelief that they would do something.

Formation: Noun + に限って; time or occasion nouns highlight an exceptional occurrence, and person nouns can introduce disbelief.

Usage and cautions: This often points to an inconvenient coincidence: the bus is late exactly when you are in a hurry. With a trusted person, あの人に限って…ない conveys that this person is surely not an offender. Do not equate every に限って with neutral “only”.

examples.ja: 急いでいる日に限って、電車が遅れます。
examples.en: The train is late precisely on days when I am in a hurry.

examples.ja: 傘を持たない日に限って、雨が降ります。
examples.reading: かさをもたないひにかぎって、あめがふります。
examples.en: It rains precisely on days when I do not bring an umbrella.

examples.ja: 彼に限って、そんなうそはつかないでしょう。
examples.reading: かれにかぎって、そんなうそはつかないでしょう。
examples.en: Surely he, of all people, would not tell such a lie.

questions.prompt: Choose the recurring unlucky exception.
choices: 急ぐ日に限らず
急ぐ日にわたって
急ぐ日に応じて
急ぐ日に限って
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “急ぐ日に限って”. に限って highlights the especially inconvenient occasion.

questions.prompt: Choose the unlucky coincidence: 大事な会議の日＿、寝坊した。
choices: に応じて
に伴って
に限って
に限らず
questions.explanation: に限って highlights oversleeping precisely on the particularly important meeting day.

questions.prompt: With a trusted colleague, あの人に限って不正はしない expresses what?
choices: A neutral description of a timetable
Disbelief that this particular person would cheat
A claim that only that person cheats
A general rule banning all work
questions.explanation: The person-focused に限って singles out someone the speaker trusts as an unlikely wrongdoer.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 傘を持たない日に限って、雨が降ります。
choices: It rains precisely on days when I do not bring an umbrella.
It never rains when I forget my umbrella.
I bring an umbrella only after it stops raining.
Rain falls regardless of the day in this statement.
questions.explanation: “傘を持たない日に限って、雨が降ります。” means “It rains precisely on days when I do not bring an umbrella.” in this example. This often points to an inconvenient coincidence: the bus is late exactly when you are in a hurry.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 彼に限って、そんなうそはつかないでしょう。
choices: He is the only person certain to tell that lie.
He has admitted telling the lie many times.
He is forbidden to speak at all.
Surely he, of all people, would not tell such a lie.
questions.explanation: “彼に限って、そんなうそはつかないでしょう。” means “Surely he, of all people, would not tell such a lie.” in this example. This often points to an inconvenient coincidence: the bus is late exactly when you are in a hurry.

grammar.title: Regardless of: にかかわらず
grammar.explanation:
Noun or paired alternatives + にかかわらず means regardless of a condition or distinction. It is common in eligibility and policy statements.

Formation: Noun or paired alternatives + にかかわらず. Examples include 年齢にかかわらず and 行く行かないにかかわらず.

Usage and cautions: The stated condition does not alter the result or eligibility. This is formal policy language, not an adjustment according to the condition. Distinguish にもかかわらず, which means despite a fact and marks an unexpected contrast. Here the condition is simply irrelevant.

examples.ja: 年齢にかかわらず、誰でも参加できます。
examples.en: Anyone can participate regardless of age.

examples.ja: 天候にかかわらず、行事は行います。
examples.reading: てんこうにかかわらず、ぎょうじはおこないます。
examples.en: The event will be held regardless of the weather.

examples.ja: 国籍にかかわらず、応募できます。
examples.reading: こくせきにかかわらず、おうぼできます。
examples.en: You can apply regardless of nationality.

questions.prompt: Choose a condition that does not affect eligibility.
choices: 経験の有無に反して
経験の有無のためにだけ
経験の有無にかかわらず
経験の有無に応じて
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “経験の有無にかかわらず”. にかかわらず makes the presence or absence of experience irrelevant.

questions.prompt: Make gender irrelevant to eligibility: 性別＿、参加できます。
choices: を皮切りに
にかかわらず
に応じてだけ
に反して
questions.explanation: にかかわらず says participation does not depend on gender; it does not prescribe different treatment by gender.

questions.prompt: Which contrasts correctly with に応じて?
choices: にかかわらず ignores the distinction; に応じて adjusts to it.
Both always mean adjusting to differences.
にかかわらず means only one category qualifies.
に応じて always prohibits a change.
questions.explanation: にかかわらず makes the condition irrelevant, while に応じて describes a response corresponding to the condition.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 天候にかかわらず、行事は行います。
choices: The event will be held only in good weather.
The event is canceled because of the weather.
The weather changes according to the event.
The event will be held regardless of the weather.
questions.explanation: “天候にかかわらず、行事は行います。” means “The event will be held regardless of the weather.” in this example. The stated condition does not alter the result or eligibility.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 国籍にかかわらず、応募できます。
choices: Nationality is decided after applying.
Nobody of any nationality may apply.
You can apply regardless of nationality.
Only citizens of one country may apply.
questions.explanation: “国籍にかかわらず、応募できます。” means “You can apply regardless of nationality.” in this example. The stated condition does not alter the result or eligibility.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: According to: に応じて
grammar.explanation:
Noun + に応じて describes an appropriate adjustment corresponding to differences or changes. It often appears with needs, ability, or circumstances.

Formation: Noun + に応じて; noun-modifying form に応じた + noun.

Usage and cautions: A response or arrangement changes appropriately with ability, demand, need or circumstance. Unlike にかかわらず, the condition matters. Unlike に伴って, this often emphasizes a suitable response rather than merely accompanying social changes. Avoid using it for an unrelated coincidence.

examples.ja: 能力に応じて、クラスを分けます。
examples.en: We divide classes according to ability.

examples.ja: 収入に応じて、税額が変わります。
examples.reading: しゅうにゅうにおうじて、ぜいがくがかわります。
examples.en: The amount of tax changes according to income.

examples.ja: 必要に応じて、説明を追加します。
examples.reading: ひつようにおうじて、せつめいをついかします。
examples.en: We will add explanations as needed.

questions.prompt: Choose an adjustment matching demand.
choices: 需要なくして増やす
需要に応じて増やす
需要に反して増やす
需要を問わず増やす
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “需要に応じて増やす”. に応じて means increasing in correspondence with demand.

questions.prompt: Modify a noun: 経験に＿仕事を任せます。
choices: 応じた
応じてのに
応じるな
応じだ
questions.explanation: に応じた modifies the following noun 仕事, describing work suited to the person’s experience.

questions.prompt: Choose adjustment to class size.
choices: 人数にかかわらず、同じ部屋を使う。
人数をよそに、何もしない。
人数に反して、予想が外れる。
人数に応じて、部屋を変える。
questions.explanation: に応じて changes the room to match the number of people; the alternatives express disregard or an unrelated contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 収入に応じて、税額が変わります。
choices: Income changes only after tax disappears.
Everyone pays no tax regardless of income.
The amount of tax changes according to income.
The amount of tax is unaffected by income.
questions.explanation: “収入に応じて、税額が変わります。” means “The amount of tax changes according to income.” in this example. A response or arrangement changes appropriately with ability, demand, need or circumstance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 必要に応じて、説明を追加します。
choices: The need for explanations disappeared yesterday.
We will add explanations as needed.
We will remove explanations regardless of need.
Explanations are never allowed to change.
questions.explanation: “必要に応じて、説明を追加します。” means “We will add explanations as needed.” in this example. A response or arrangement changes appropriately with ability, demand, need or circumstance.

grammar.source: Original curriculum; CC BY-SA 4.0. Level placement is an estimate, not an official JLPT syllabus.

grammar.title: Parallel change: に伴って
grammar.explanation:
Noun or dictionary verb + に伴って links changes that accompany one another. It can describe social trends rather than a single deliberate response.

Formation: Noun or dictionary verb + に伴って / に伴い. Before a noun use に伴う.

Usage and cautions: This links related changes, often demographic, economic or institutional. The second development accompanies the first rather than necessarily being a consciously chosen response. It can also describe duties accompanying a position. Do not confuse accompaniment with chronological “before”.

examples.ja: 人口の増加に伴って、住宅が増えました。
examples.en: Housing increased along with population growth.

examples.ja: 気温の上昇に伴って、電力の使用量が増えました。
examples.reading: きおんのじょうしょうにともなって、でんりょくのしようりょうがふえました。
examples.en: Electricity use increased along with rising temperatures.

examples.ja: 駅の完成に伴い、周辺の店が増えました。

高齢化に先立って
高齢化に限って
高齢化をよそに

を問わず
に限ってだけ

grammar.title: Contrary to: に反して
grammar.explanation:
Noun + に反して introduces a result opposing expectations, intentions, or rules. It is not simply a contrast between two unrelated facts.

Formation: Noun + に反して; noun-modifying form に反する + noun. Often paired with 予想, 期待, 意志 or 規則.

Usage and cautions: The outcome goes against a prediction, wish or standard. It is not merely two different facts. Unlike に応じて, the second fact does not appropriately match the first. For violation of rules, に反する can directly modify 行為 or another noun.

examples.ja: 予想に反して、売上が伸びました。
examples.en: Contrary to expectations, sales grew.

examples.ja: 予想に反して、試験は簡単でした。
examples.reading: よそうにはんして、しけんはかんたんでした。
examples.en: Contrary to expectations, the exam was easy.

examples.ja: 親の希望に反して、彼は海外で働く道を選びました。
examples.reading: おやのきぼうにはんして、かれはかいがいではたらくみちをえらびました。
examples.en: Against his parents’ wishes, he chose to work abroad.

questions.prompt: Complete 'contrary to expectations'.
choices: 期待に応じて
期待に先立って
期待に伴って
期待に反して
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “期待に反して”. に反して marks the result as opposing the expected direction.

questions.prompt: Describe conduct violating rules: 規則に＿行為。
choices: 反しの
反したらの
反する
反してな
questions.explanation: に反する is the noun-modifying form before 行為, meaning conduct contrary to the rules.

questions.prompt: Choose a result opposing a forecast.
choices: 予報を聞きながら、支度した。
予報に反して、晴れた。
予報どおり、雨が降った。
予報を確認するために、出かけた。
questions.explanation: 予報に反して means the weather differed from the forecast, unlike 予報どおり which confirms it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 予想に反して、試験は簡単でした。
choices: Contrary to expectations, the exam was easy.
The exam was easy exactly as expected.
I expected the exam only after taking it.
The exam is not scheduled yet.
questions.explanation: “予想に反して、試験は簡単でした。” means “Contrary to expectations, the exam was easy.” in this example. The outcome goes against a prediction, wish or standard.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 親の希望に反して、彼は海外で働く道を選びました。
choices: Following his parents’ wishes, he stayed at home.
His parents chose to work abroad instead of him.
He cannot work abroad because he has no choice.
Against his parents’ wishes, he chose to work abroad.
questions.explanation: “親の希望に反して、彼は海外で働く道を選びました。” means “Against his parents’ wishes, he chose to work abroad.” in this example. The outcome goes against a prediction, wish or standard.

grammar.title: Despite an expected standard: わりに
grammar.explanation:
Plain clause or noun + の followed by わりに notes a mismatch with the standard expected from a fact. It is usually milder than くせに.

Formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + わりに; noun + のわりに; な-adjective + なわりに.

Usage and cautions: This evaluates a result against the normal standard expected from a fact. The mismatch can be positive or negative. It is usually less openly reproachful than くせに, but judgments about someone’s age or status may still be tactless. It does not merely give a cause.

examples.ja: この店は高いわりに、おいしくありません。
examples.en: For such an expensive restaurant, the food is not very good.

examples.ja: この靴は安いわりに、丈夫です。
examples.reading: このくつはやすいわりに、じょうぶです。
examples.en: These shoes are durable for their low price.

examples.ja: 練習したわりに、うまくできませんでした。
examples.reading: れんしゅうしたわりに、うまくできませんでした。
examples.en: Considering how much I practiced, I did not do very well.

questions.prompt: Choose the link after a noun: 値段＿質がいい。
choices: だわりに
でわりに
のわりに
なわりに
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “のわりに”. Nouns take の before わりに; the quality exceeds what the price suggests.

questions.prompt: Complete a な-adjective comparison: 不便＿わりに、家賃が高い。
choices: に
な
の
だ
questions.explanation: 不便 is a な-adjective, so it takes な before わりに; the rent is high given the inconvenience.

questions.prompt: Which nuance best fits 高いわりに質が悪い?
choices: The quality is poor relative to the high price.
The high price guarantees good quality.
The price must be lowered by law.
The quality caused the price to rise yesterday.
questions.explanation: わりに compares actual quality with the standard expected from a high price and notes a mismatch.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この靴は安いわりに、丈夫です。
choices: These shoes break easily because they are expensive.
These shoes are cheap because they are broken.
These shoes are expensive and fragile as expected.
These shoes are durable for their low price.
questions.explanation: “この靴は安いわりに、丈夫です。” means “These shoes are durable for their low price.” in this example. This evaluates a result against the normal standard expected from a fact.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 練習したわりに、うまくできませんでした。
choices: I could not practice because I did well.
I did well exactly as much as expected from practice.
Considering how much I practiced, I did not do very well.
I performed perfectly without practicing.
questions.explanation: “練習したわりに、うまくできませんでした。” means “Considering how much I practiced, I did not do very well.” in this example. This evaluates a result against the normal standard expected from a fact.

grammar.title: Criticism: くせに
grammar.explanation:
Clause + くせに expresses critical or reproachful contrast. Use it cautiously about other people; it is not a neutral equivalent of 'although'.

Formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + くせに; noun + のくせに; な-adjective + なくせに.

Usage and cautions: This expresses blame, contempt or irritation at a contradiction. It is inappropriate as a neutral formal “although”, especially about a superior. The two clauses normally concern the same person or entity. Use のに or わりに when critical reproach is not intended.

examples.ja: 知っているくせに、教えてくれません。
examples.en: Despite knowing, they will not tell me.

examples.ja: 知っているくせに、知らないふりをしています。
examples.reading: しっているくせに、しらないふりをしています。
examples.en: Although they know, they are pretending not to.

examples.ja: 約束したくせに、来ませんでした。
examples.reading: やくそくしたくせに、きませんでした。
examples.en: They did not come, even though they had promised.

questions.prompt: Which nuance does くせに often carry?
choices: A request for permission
Blame or criticism
A neutral time sequence
Respectful gratitude
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “Blame or criticism”. くせに conveys a negative judgment about the contradiction.

questions.prompt: Complete a noun reproach: 専門家＿くせに、基本も知らない。
choices: の
な
だ
を
questions.explanation: A noun takes の before くせに; the sentence reproachfully contrasts expert status with ignorance.

questions.prompt: Which connector is unsuitable for a neutral, respectful report?
choices: 一方で
ものの
にもかかわらず
くせに
questions.explanation: くせに carries reproach or contempt, unlike the more neutral contrastive options.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 知っているくせに、知らないふりをしています。
choices: They learned it only after pretending.
They are kindly teaching everything they know.
Although they know, they are pretending not to.
They honestly do not know and admit it.
questions.explanation: “知っているくせに、知らないふりをしています。” means “Although they know, they are pretending not to.” in this example. This expresses blame, contempt or irritation at a contradiction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 約束したくせに、来ませんでした。
choices: They promised only after arriving.
They did not come, even though they had promised.
They came precisely as they had promised.
They never made a promise to come.
questions.explanation: “約束したくせに、来ませんでした。” means “They did not come, even though they had promised.” in this example. This expresses blame, contempt or irritation at a contradiction.

grammar.title: Not only: ばかりか
grammar.explanation:
Plain clause + ばかりか adds a further, often stronger fact. Nouns and な-adjectives can use であるばかりか in formal language.

Formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + ばかりか; nouns can attach directly or use であるばかりか in formal predicates.

Usage and cautions: The second fact adds to, and often intensifies, the first. も or まで can highlight the addition. This is not a simple reason or a sequence of mutually exclusive alternatives. Both positive achievements and compounded problems can use the pattern.

examples.ja: 彼は英語ばかりか、中国語も話せます。
examples.en: He speaks not only English but also Chinese.

examples.ja: この店は安いばかりか、配達も無料です。
examples.reading: このみせはやすいばかりか、はいたつもむりょうです。
examples.en: This shop is not only inexpensive; delivery is free too.

examples.ja: 彼女は歌うばかりか、作曲もします。
examples.reading: かのじょはうたうばかりか、さっきょくもします。
examples.en: She not only sings but also composes music.

questions.prompt: Choose an additive escalation.
choices: 遅刻したばかりか、資料も忘れた
遅刻しただけに、資料を用意した
遅刻する前に、資料を読んだ
遅刻したので、急いだ
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “遅刻したばかりか、資料も忘れた”. ばかりか adds forgetting the materials to the initial problem.

questions.prompt: Add a further problem: 雨が降った＿、風まで強くなった。
choices: だけなので
からには必ず
ためだけに
ばかりか
questions.explanation: ばかりか adds the worsening wind to the rain, and まで reinforces the escalation.

questions.prompt: What relationship does ばかりか normally express?
choices: A direct prohibition
An unfulfilled wish only
An additional fact beyond the first
A necessary deadline
questions.explanation: ばかりか means not only the first fact but also another, often stronger or more surprising fact.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: この店は安いばかりか、配達も無料です。
choices: The shop became expensive after delivery stopped.
This shop is not only inexpensive; delivery is free too.
The shop is inexpensive because delivery is costly.
Only delivery is free; everything else is expensive.
questions.explanation: “この店は安いばかりか、配達も無料です。” means “This shop is not only inexpensive; delivery is free too.” in this example. The second fact adds to, and often intensifies, the first.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 彼女は歌うばかりか、作曲もします。
choices: She not only sings but also composes music.
She composes instead of ever singing.
She can neither sing nor compose.
She sings only when someone else composes.
questions.explanation: “彼女は歌うばかりか、作曲もします。” means “She not only sings but also composes music.” in this example. The second fact adds to, and often intensifies, the first.

grammar.title: Rather than: どころか
grammar.explanation:
どころか rejects the first description as inadequate and introduces a contrasting or much stronger reality. Context can make the second fact opposite in direction.

Formation: Plain verb / い-adjective or noun / な-adjective stem + どころか. The second clause overturns or surpasses the first description.

Usage and cautions: This can move to an opposite fact or to a much greater degree. Far from being easy, it is difficult; far from merely walking, someone can run. It is stronger than a neutral addition. Do not retain な before a noun-like adjective in the basic 簡単どころか pattern.

examples.ja: 休むどころか、昼食を食べる時間もありません。
examples.en: Far from resting, I do not even have time for lunch.

examples.ja: 涼しいどころか、寒いくらいです。
examples.reading: すずしいどころか、さむいくらいです。
examples.en: It is not merely cool; it is almost cold.

examples.ja: 旅行どころか、週末に休むこともできません。
examples.reading: りょこうどころか、しゅうまつにやすむこともできません。
examples.en: Far from traveling, I cannot even take time off on weekends.

questions.prompt: Choose 'far from easy; very difficult'.
choices: 簡単なだけに、とても難しい
簡単に限って、とても難しい
簡単なので、とても楽しい
簡単どころか、とても難しい
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “簡単どころか、とても難しい”. どころか overturns the initial description of the task as easy.

questions.prompt: Reject a positive description: 便利＿、かえって時間がかかります。
choices: だから
のために
どころか
なばかりで
questions.explanation: 便利どころか overturns the claim of convenience with the contrary result that it takes extra time.

questions.prompt: Which statement fits 回復するどころか、悪化した?
choices: The condition has never changed.
The condition worsened instead of recovering.
The condition recovered fully.
Recovery and worsening were equally desired.
questions.explanation: どころか rejects the first expected direction and introduces the opposite actual development, worsening.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 涼しいどころか、寒いくらいです。
choices: It is not merely cool; it is almost cold.
It is neither cool nor cold, but very hot.
It became cool because it was cold yesterday.
I would prefer cool weather to cold weather.
questions.explanation: “涼しいどころか、寒いくらいです。” means “It is not merely cool; it is almost cold.” in this example. This can move to an opposite fact or to a much greater degree.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 旅行どころか、週末に休むこともできません。
choices: I can travel freely every weekend.
I rested all weekend after traveling.
I cannot travel because weekends are too relaxing.
Far from traveling, I cannot even take time off on weekends.
questions.explanation: “旅行どころか、週末に休むこともできません。” means “Far from traveling, I cannot even take time off on weekends.” in this example. This can move to an opposite fact or to a much greater degree.

grammar.title: No choice: ざるを得ない
grammar.explanation:
Use the negative stem + ざるを得ない to express being forced by circumstances to act. The irregular form for する is せざるを得ない.

Formation: Negative stem + ざるを得ない: 行かざるを得ない, 食べざるを得ない. する exceptionally becomes せざるを得ない.

Usage and cautions: External circumstances leave no acceptable alternative. This is formal and often implies reluctance, not an enthusiastic wish. For godan verbs ending in う, use わ: 買わざるを得ない. It is a fixed double-negative expression; do not build it with the potential stem.

examples.ja: 電車が止まり、タクシーを使わざるを得ませんでした。
examples.en: The trains stopped, so I had no choice but to take a taxi.

examples.ja: 予算が足りず、計画を縮小せざるを得ません。
examples.reading: よさんがたりず、けいかくをしゅくしょうせざるをえません。
examples.en: Because the budget is insufficient, we have no choice but to scale down the plan.

examples.ja: 終電を逃し、歩いて帰らざるを得ませんでした。
examples.reading: しゅうでんをのがし、あるいてかえらざるをえませんでした。
examples.en: I missed the last train and had no choice but to walk home.

questions.prompt: Choose the form for する.
choices: すざるを得ない
するざるを得ない
せざるを得ない
しざるを得ない
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “せざるを得ない”. する exceptionally becomes せ before ざるを得ない.

questions.prompt: Choose the form of 買う.
choices: 買えざるを得ない
買わざるを得ない
買いざるを得ない
買うざるを得ない
questions.explanation: The negative stem of 買う is 買わ-, as in 買わない; attach ざるを得ない to that stem.

questions.prompt: Which context best fits 変更せざるを得ない?
choices: Unexpected flooding makes the original route impossible.
Everyone freely prefers the original route.
Changing routes is strictly forbidden.
The route has never been planned.
questions.explanation: ざるを得ない presents a compelled change when circumstances remove practical alternatives.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 予算が足りず、計画を縮小せざるを得ません。
choices: We have enough money and eagerly choose to expand the plan.
We are not allowed to change the plan under any circumstances.
The plan has already been completed without any change.
Because the budget is insufficient, we have no choice but to scale down the plan.
questions.explanation: “予算が足りず、計画を縮小せざるを得ません。” means “Because the budget is insufficient, we have no choice but to scale down the plan.” in this example. External circumstances leave no acceptable alternative.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 終電を逃し、歩いて帰らざるを得ませんでした。
choices: I chose to walk home for fun before the last train.
I was forbidden to walk home after missing the train.
I missed the last train and had no choice but to walk home.
I caught the last train and did not walk home.
questions.explanation: “終電を逃し、歩いて帰らざるを得ませんでした。” means “I missed the last train and had no choice but to walk home.” in this example. External circumstances leave no acceptable alternative.

grammar.title: Cannot fail to feel: ずにはいられない
grammar.explanation:
Negative stem + ずにはいられない expresses an uncontrollable impulse to act or feel. する becomes せずにはいられない.

Formation: Negative stem + ずにはいられない. する→せずにはいられない; 来る→来ずにはいられない.

Usage and cautions: An emotion or impulse makes restraint impossible. It differs from external necessity in ざるを得ない. Common verbs include 笑う, 泣く and 心配する. A past ending describes an impulse that could not be suppressed at the time, not a standing legal duty.

examples.ja: その話を聞いて、泣かずにはいられませんでした。
examples.en: Hearing that story, I could not help crying.

examples.ja: その冗談を聞いて、笑わずにはいられませんでした。
examples.reading: そのじょうだんをきいて、わらわずにはいられませんでした。
examples.en: Hearing that joke, I could not help laughing.

examples.ja: 連絡がないと、心配せずにはいられません。
examples.reading: れんらくがないと、しんぱいせずにはいられません。
examples.en: When there is no contact, I cannot help worrying.

questions.prompt: What does 笑わずにはいられない mean?
choices: Choose not to laugh freely
Cannot help laughing
Must never laugh
Have never laughed
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “Cannot help laughing”. The double-negative construction describes an irresistible impulse.

questions.prompt: Choose the form with する.
choices: 質問せずにはいられない
質問しずにはいられない
質問するずにはいられない
質問できずにはいられない
questions.explanation: する uses the exceptional negative stem せ before ず: 質問せずにはいられない means cannot help asking.

questions.prompt: Which distinguishes this from ざるを得ない?
choices: It always describes a legal obligation.
It forbids the action absolutely.
It means the action has never occurred.
It emphasizes an irresistible inner impulse.
questions.explanation: ずにはいられない foregrounds inability to restrain an impulse; ざるを得ない often foregrounds external constraints.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: その冗談を聞いて、笑わずにはいられませんでした。
choices: I was ordered never to laugh at that joke.
I had never heard a joke before.
Hearing that joke, I could not help laughing.
Hearing that joke, I managed not to laugh at all.
questions.explanation: “その冗談を聞いて、笑わずにはいられませんでした。” means “Hearing that joke, I could not help laughing.” in this example. An emotion or impulse makes restraint impossible.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 連絡がないと、心配せずにはいられません。
choices: I choose not to worry regardless of contact.
When there is no contact, I cannot help worrying.
No contact makes it impossible for me to worry.
I am forbidden to contact anyone who worries.
questions.explanation: “連絡がないと、心配せずにはいられません。” means “When there is no contact, I cannot help worrying.” in this example. An emotion or impulse makes restraint impossible.

grammar.title: Possible risk: かねない
grammar.explanation:
Verb stem + かねない means an undesirable result could occur. Do not confuse it with かねる, which often politely expresses inability.

Formation: Verb ます-stem + かねない; polite かねません. This warns that an undesirable outcome is possible.

Usage and cautions: Despite its negative-looking ending, かねない means the event could happen. It is not the polite inability expressed by かねる. Use it for risks, not as the ordinary way to predict an eagerly desired success. Context should make the negative consequence clear.

examples.ja: このままでは事故が起こりかねません。
examples.en: At this rate an accident could occur.

examples.ja: このまま無理をすると、体を壊しかねません。
examples.reading: このままむりをすると、からだをこわしかねません。
examples.en: If you keep overdoing it, you could damage your health.

examples.ja: 確認を怠ると、大きな誤解を招きかねません。
examples.reading: かくにんをおこたると、おおきなごかいをまねきかねません。
examples.en: Neglecting to check could lead to a serious misunderstanding.

questions.prompt: Which warns of a negative possibility?
choices: 失敗しかねない
失敗しかねる
失敗しきる
失敗しないで済む
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “失敗しかねない”. しかねない warns of a possible bad outcome; しかねる means cannot readily do.

questions.prompt: Warn about a data-loss risk: 操作を間違えると、データが消え＿。
choices: かねる
きる
たい
かねない
questions.explanation: 消え is the stem of 消える; 消えかねない warns that data might disappear.

questions.prompt: What does 事故につながりかねません express?
choices: An accident has definitely happened.
Someone wishes for an accident.
There is a risk of an accident.
An accident cannot occur.
questions.explanation: かねません is the polite form of かねない and warns of a possible unwelcome consequence.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: このまま無理をすると、体を壊しかねません。
choices: You must damage your health to keep working.
If you keep overdoing it, you could damage your health.
If you keep overdoing it, your health is guaranteed to improve.
You are unable to damage your health under any conditions.
questions.explanation: “このまま無理をすると、体を壊しかねません。” means “If you keep overdoing it, you could damage your health.” in this example. Despite its negative-looking ending, かねない means the event could happen.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 確認を怠ると、大きな誤解を招きかねません。
choices: Neglecting to check could lead to a serious misunderstanding.
Checking carefully always causes a serious misunderstanding.
A misunderstanding is impossible even without checking.
You must invite someone to check a large object.
questions.explanation: “確認を怠ると、大きな誤解を招きかねません。” means “Neglecting to check could lead to a serious misunderstanding.” in this example. Despite its negative-looking ending, かねない means the event could happen.

grammar.title: Unable to comply: かねる
grammar.explanation:
Verb stem + かねる is a formal way to say one cannot readily do something, often for policy or psychological reasons rather than physical incapacity.

Formation: Verb ます-stem + かねる. Polite refusal commonly uses かねます: お答えしかねます.

Usage and cautions: This signals difficulty in complying, deciding or doing something, often because of policy or hesitation. It is softer and more formal than a blunt できない. Do not attach the full ます form. Distinguish かねない, which predicts a possible undesirable result.

examples.ja: そのご要望にはお応えしかねます。
examples.en: We are unable to meet that request.

examples.ja: 個人情報のため、お答えしかねます。
examples.reading: こじんじょうほうのため、おこたえしかねます。
examples.en: Because it is personal information, we are unable to answer.

examples.ja: 情報が少なく、今は判断しかねます。
examples.reading: じょうほうがすくなく、いまははんだんしかねます。
examples.en: There is little information, so I cannot readily make a judgment now.

questions.prompt: What does 判断しかねる convey?
choices: A judgment is likely to cause harm
Have completely finished judging
Want to judge immediately
Cannot readily make a judgment
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “Cannot readily make a judgment”. かねる expresses difficulty or inability to comply.

questions.prompt: Form a polite inability to agree: その案には賛成し＿。
choices: きりました
そうでした
かねます
かねません
questions.explanation: 賛成しかねます formally says one cannot agree; しかねません would suggest a possibility of agreeing.

questions.prompt: Which is a restrained formal refusal to refund?
choices: 返金には応じたいです。
返金には応じかねます。
返金には応じかねません。
返金には応じてみます。
questions.explanation: 応じかねます expresses inability to comply with the refund request, unlike possibility, trial or desire.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 個人情報のため、お答えしかねます。
choices: Because it is personal information, we are unable to answer.
Because it is personal information, we may accidentally answer.
We have already answered every personal question.
Please answer without considering personal information.
questions.explanation: “個人情報のため、お答えしかねます。” means “Because it is personal information, we are unable to answer.” in this example. This signals difficulty in complying, deciding or doing something, often because of policy or hesitation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 情報が少なく、今は判断しかねます。
choices: There is plenty of information, so my judgment is final.
I may accidentally lose all the information now.
I refuse ever to obtain any information.
There is little information, so I cannot readily make a judgment now.
questions.explanation: “情報が少なく、今は判断しかねます。” means “There is little information, so I cannot readily make a judgment now.” in this example. This signals difficulty in complying, deciding or doing something, often because of policy or hesitation.

grammar.title: Not necessarily: とは限らない
grammar.explanation:
Clause + とは限らない denies that a proposition always holds. Often used with 必ずしも to challenge a generalization.

Formation: Plain proposition + とは限らない. Often paired with 必ずしも to deny a universal assumption.

Usage and cautions: The statement may be true in some cases and false in others. It does not assert the opposite universally. Retain the proposition before と: 成功するとは限らない. This is useful for correcting overgeneralizations, not for issuing a direct prohibition.

examples.ja: 高い物が必ずしも良いとは限りません。
examples.en: Expensive things are not necessarily good.

examples.ja: 有名な店がおいしいとは限りません。
examples.reading: ゆうめいなみせがおいしいとはかぎりません。
examples.en: Famous restaurants are not necessarily good.

examples.ja: 日本に住んでいても、日本語が話せるとは限りません。
examples.reading: にほんにすんでいても、にほんごがはなせるとはかぎりません。
examples.en: Even living in Japan does not necessarily mean one can speak Japanese.

questions.prompt: Choose partial denial of a rule.
choices: 努力すれば必ず成功する
努力したことがない
努力すれば必ず成功するとは限らない
努力しても絶対に成功しない
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “努力すれば必ず成功するとは限らない”. とは限らない leaves room for both success and failure.

questions.prompt: Deny a guarantee: 安い物はすぐ壊れる＿。
choices: というものだ
とは限らない
に決まっている
はずだ
questions.explanation: とは限らない rejects the universal claim that inexpensive goods break quickly, without claiming they never break.

questions.prompt: Which paraphrase matches 必ず成功するとは限らない?
choices: Success is not guaranteed.
Failure is guaranteed.
Success has already happened.
Trying is forbidden.
questions.explanation: The construction denies guaranteed success and leaves both success and failure possible.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 有名な店がおいしいとは限りません。
choices: Famous restaurants are always bad.
Every famous restaurant is definitely good.
Famous restaurants are forbidden from serving food.
Famous restaurants are not necessarily good.
questions.explanation: “有名な店がおいしいとは限りません。” means “Famous restaurants are not necessarily good.” in this example. The statement may be true in some cases and false in others.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 日本に住んでいても、日本語が話せるとは限りません。
choices: Everyone living in Japan certainly speaks Japanese.
Speaking Japanese is a requirement for every trip.
Even living in Japan does not necessarily mean one can speak Japanese.
Nobody living in Japan can speak Japanese.
questions.explanation: “日本に住んでいても、日本語が話せるとは限りません。” means “Even living in Japan does not necessarily mean one can speak Japanese.” in this example. The statement may be true in some cases and false in others.

grammar.title: Whether or not: にしても
grammar.explanation:
にしても can concede a premise before qualification, or appear in AにしてもBにしても to cover alternatives. It is not always a simple conditional.

Formation: Plain clause + にしても for a conceded premise. AにしてもBにしても covers either alternative.

Usage and cautions: The speaker grants a condition provisionally but adds a reservation, criticism or conclusion. With alternatives, the conclusion applies whichever is chosen. Do not interpret every instance as an actual settled fact. This differs from にしては, which judges something against an expected standard.

examples.ja: 忙しいにしても、連絡ぐらいはできるでしょう。
examples.en: Even if you are busy, you could at least get in touch.

examples.ja: 疲れているにしても、挨拶ぐらいはしてください。
examples.reading: つかれているにしても、あいさつぐらいはしてください。
examples.en: Even if you are tired, please at least say hello.

examples.ja: 行くにしても行かないにしても、今日中に連絡してください。
examples.reading: いくにしてもいかないにしても、きょうじゅうにれんらくしてください。
examples.en: Whether you go or not, please let me know today.

questions.prompt: Which concedes a premise before criticism?
choices: 知らなかったので、何もしなくてよい
知らなかったにしても、確認すべきだった
知らないために、確認しなかった
知らないうちに、終わった
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “知らなかったにしても、確認すべきだった”. にしても accepts the premise provisionally without accepting the resulting behavior.

questions.prompt: Concede cost but reject excess: 高い＿、十万円は高すぎます。
choices: にしても
ためにだけ
ようにだけ
ばかりでなく
questions.explanation: 高いにしても grants that it may be expensive, then qualifies that ten万円 is still excessive.

questions.prompt: In 買うにしても借りるにしても, what does the repeated pattern cover?
choices: Only buying, excluding borrowing
Only a past completed purchase
A prohibition on both actions
Both buying and borrowing as alternatives
questions.explanation: AにしてもBにしても makes the following conclusion apply under either alternative.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 疲れているにしても、挨拶ぐらいはしてください。
choices: Please become tired before greeting anyone.
You said hello only after fully recovering.
Even if you are tired, please at least say hello.
Because you are tired, you must not say hello.
questions.explanation: “疲れているにしても、挨拶ぐらいはしてください。” means “Even if you are tired, please at least say hello.” in this example. The speaker grants a condition provisionally but adds a reservation, criticism or conclusion.

questions.prompt: Choose the best English meaning: 行くにしても行かないにしても、今日中に連絡してください。
choices: Contact me only after you return tomorrow.
Whether you go or not, please let me know today.
Please contact me today only if you go.
You must go today without contacting me.
questions.explanation: “行くにしても行かないにしても、今日中に連絡してください。” means “Whether you go or not, please let me know today.” in this example. The speaker grants a condition provisionally but adds a reservation, criticism or conclusion.
